_notes: ops-hardening iter-50 audit-fix pass 2, finding T3. The previous golden was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of passing: step 5 waited 15,000 ms for a job the lane itself measured at 11m16s, so steps 6-8 asserted against a still-running job every time. Two things were confirmed before this rewrite rather than assumed:

(a) demo_runner.py's 20,000 ms hard cap applies to a step's LOCATOR/expect timeout (`tmo`), NOT to `wait_for {ms}` — `_do_action` passes that value straight to `page.wait_for_timeout(...)`. Verified empirically on 2026-08-06 with a throwaway J-99 golden carrying `wait_for {ms: 45000}`: the verify run took 47 s wall and returned PASS. The iter-49 conclusion recorded in the phase spec's OUT OF SCOPE ('no wait value can cover an 11-minute job') generalised the locator cap too far.

(b) Wait sizing: the same in-app backfill measured 11m16s (iter-50), 18m18s (2026-08-06, concurrent with a factor-lab compute), and 18m13s (ops-hardening iter-58 browser-qa live run, 2026-08-10T20:06:45Z-20:24:56Z, job data_provider_runs.id=382, date 2010-11-04, aggregates_refreshed all 9 categories). 1,200,000 ms (20 min) covers all three measurements with margin.

Golden discipline (iter-47/48 lessons): steps 10/12/14/15 no longer rest on page-wide text a persisted history panel could satisfy regardless of outcome. Step 10 asserts THIS run's own breakdown counts (a re-run over an already-snapshotted day renders '1 already snapshotted' and FAILS here — the assertion has teeth); step 12 asserts TC-10's `aggregates_refreshed` list, never asserted before; step 14 CLICKS the date's own link through to /scanner-runs/<run_id> and asserts that run detail's own header; step 15 asserts the stored leaderboard table actually rendered (the real column header, 'ENTRY QUALITY' — confirmed uppercase in the live-rendered DOM this pass, corrected from the earlier lower-case 'Entry Quality' text which does not appear verbatim on this page) rather than the 'No stored stock rows' empty state.

Single-use by construction: the target date must have 0 snapshot rows when this runs (J-05's own defining case is an UNSNAPSHOTTED day). The first rotation note in this pass was itself stale within the hour — which is the standing lesson below, demonstrated twice in one dispatch: re-verify live before clicking Start; this file's prose is not evidence.

Wait sizing, FOURTH and FIFTH measurements (ops-hardening iter-59 audit-fix pass, both on this same host, same day): 17m04.5s (03:48:33.994Z -> 04:05:38.502Z, date 2010-11-05, data_provider_runs.id=389) and 25m13.7s (04:08:04.395Z -> 04:33:18.058Z, date 2010-11-15, data_provider_runs.id=390, the run this golden's own PASS rests on). The five measured durations are now 11m16s / 18m18s / 18m13s / 17m04s / 25m14s. The 25m14s run finished with roughly TWO SECONDS to spare against the 1,500,000 ms (25 min) wait this pass had just raised it to — a pass that close is luck, not margin, and the trend across the five is upward because each new snapshot date invalidates the dataset version and forces the whole finalize tail (factor_lab_all_warm alone took 607s in the measured run) to re-warm. Raised to 2,400,000 ms (40 min). The wait is a FLOOR on the replay's wall time, not a timeout: too large costs only lane minutes when the job finishes early, too small silently asserts against a still-running job and reports a FAIL that is really a fixture defect — the exact iter-50 T3 failure this golden was rewritten to remove.

ops-hardening iter-64 (developer): implemented the structural fix the note directly above called for. Steps 2/3's fill targets, steps 13/14 (goto-expect text, click-target text, and the post-click 'Immutable snapshot — as of ...' expect text), and the journey's own `name` field no longer carry a hand-picked literal date — every one of them now carries the run-time sentinel token `{{AUTO_UNSNAPSHOTTED_DATE}}`. `demo_runner.py` (`resolve_sentinel_date`/`resolve_and_substitute_sentinel`, wired into both `run_verify` and `main()` ahead of `run_record`/`run_live`) resolves the token EXACTLY ONCE per replay, immediately before this golden's steps run, via a read-only query against apps/backend/data/trendora.db: the earliest `daily_prices` date in a bounded window (`_SENTINEL_WINDOW_START`/`_SENTINEL_WINDOW_END`, actually shipped as **2005-03-01..2016-12-31** — this note originally misstated the window as 1996-01-01..2004-12-31, a stray draft value that never matched the constants committed in this SAME change; corrected ops-hardening iter-66, TC-6, text-only) that carries ZERO `scanner_runs` rows, then substitutes that SAME resolved date into every step carrying the token in one pass. This is no longer a file-editing concern for future iterations: whichever date a run consumes is automatically excluded from the NEXT resolution (the query itself excludes any already-snapshotted date), so this golden never again needs a human (or agent) to re-verify a date live and hand-rotate this file — closing the defect this file's own `_notes` have flagged for four consecutive rounds (iter-58, iter-59 x2, iter-62/63, iter-63-audit). Proven at the unit level (`demo_runner.py self-test`: `_t_resolve_sentinel_date_self_renews_after_consumption` seeds a throwaway fixture with a `scanner_runs` row for the just-returned date and asserts the resolver's next call returns a DIFFERENT, still-unsnapshotted date) rather than via a second ~20-minute live browser replay in the same iteration — the live end-to-end proof rides on this iteration's own mandatory replay of this golden (TC-2) and on iteration 65's own natural replay, per this iteration's spec. The prior rotation history above (iter-50 through iter-63-audit) is left completely untouched — it remains the record of how this golden's target date was hand-managed before this mechanism existed; the literal date `2010-11-22` no longer appears in the executable steps.
